mechanic: A mistaken witness, not a lying one: she saw a figure and took it for a man she knew by his cloak. What she saw is kept and her identification is set aside; her mistake is itself evidence.
note: Spoilers. The logic written before the prose, in the shape sketched in docs/archipelago-plan.md. `frame` is what the narrator's own prose always carries; `clues` are the units that could be case files. `facts` names the world model's facts that realise a clue, `chain` the tellings that bring it.

frame.says: The cash drawer of the surgery was found forced on Wednesday morning, the week's takings gone.

questions.asks: Who was it that Mrs. Lunn saw at the side door?

rules_out.Dr. Mott: c.bedside: he was three miles off, in the narrator's sight
rules_out.Kitty: c.lunn_again and c.keys: the cloak cleared the ground, and she is hardly five feet tall
rules_out.anyone else: c.keys: a key to the side door

clues.source: Mrs. Lunn, who lives opposite the side door, to the narrator on Wednesday
clues.says: At nine she saw a figure come out at the side door and go off down the lane; it was the doctor, she says: she knew him by his long grey cloak.
clues.note: One fact of the three is false and sincerely meant: her identification.

clues.says: From eight until ten he sat with the doctor at the Squire's bedside, three miles off.
The doctor drove out in his greatcoat; his grey cloak was on its peg in the surgery passage on Wednesday, still damp.

clues.source: The narrator's own knowledge of the household
clues.says: Beside the doctor, the dispenser and the housemaid have keys to the side door; the housemaid is hardly five feet tall.
The cloak hung on the figure as on the doctor, well clear of the ground.
